conflicts.point: Whether pre-market safety evaluation is necessary or merely imposes bureaucratic delays that worsen human harm compared to continuous telemetry.

positions.stance: Pre-market safety gating is mandatory because post-market telemetry treats live applicants as expendable error-correction data and fails to retroactively restore damaged financial or employment standing.
Pre-market gating causes severe human toll by trapping applicants in slower, biased human review systems, whereas real-time telemetry catches bias quickly without operational bottlenecks.

conflicts.point: Whether population-level automated tripwires provide adequate oversight or constitute ambient surveillance that leaves individual victims without direct remediation.

positions.stance: Population-level metric monitoring without per-case attribution is insufficient because it fails to issue refunds or jobs to specific wrongly denied applicants.
Automated compliance agents and dynamic metric monitoring provide sufficient systemic transparency and speed without choking market access through static gatekeeping.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market safety evaluation is necessary or merely imposes bureaucratic delays that worsen human harm compared to continuous telemetry.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position offers a concrete deployment mechanism through forty-eight-hour automated tripwires. The safetyist position relies on abstract assertions about irreversible harm without detailing how pre-market review agencies will process volume without creating backlogs.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Data showing that pre-market review catches systemic flaws which automated tripwires systematically miss.

verdicts.conflict: Whether population-level automated tripwires provide adequate oversight or constitute ambient surveillance that leaves individual victims without direct remediation.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic argument addresses the full legal scope of anti-discrimination statutes by requiring per-case attribution and specific remedies like job placement or financial refunds. Systemic tripwires alone fail to satisfy current statutory requirements for individual victim compensation.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Statutory reform that replaces individual civil rights claims with class-action regulatory fines funded by systemic metric violations.
